title: A triple failure under the pair condition makes counting #P-hard at every sector order
claim: p >= 5, r | p - 1, n graded nilpotent over F_p of class at most 4 with a grading-preserving C_r action, G = exp(n) x| C_r, d | r. Under (P2_d), (P3_d) fails iff some near triple [[n_a, n_-a], n_(+-a)] is nonzero (far triples vanish by Jacobi). If (P2_d) holds and (P3_d) fails, counting |Hom(pi_1 S^3_(d/p)(K), G)| over knot diagrams K is #P-hard (Turing). Ingredients: slope d/p turns closed counts into positive sums of pinned knot-group counts, multiplicative over connected sums; Squier duality J_t with the reversed Artin identity; summands with vanishing local forms (negative amphichiral two-bridge knots b(4m^2+1, 2m) at odd-order roots, (k,1)-cables of T(2,p) at even-order roots); the steering rule kappa_t = t^-2 - t^-1 on d-strand bundles; the edge weight counts zeros of a trilinear form; sector isolation and Bulatov-Grohe. With COPRIME-DICHOTOMY-20261027-001A, TRIPLE-SYSTEM-20261027-001C and CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001C this decides every graded n of class at most 4 except those whose criterion fails at the occurring sector orders only through pair failures in class 3 or 4.
failure_conditions: A graded algebra satisfying (P2_d) with a nonzero far triple, or a nonzero Lie monomial of nontrivial-character elements whose character violates the parity rule.

A letter or n for which Bur_(1/t)(g)^T J_t Bur_t(g) != J_t, a braid for which the reversed Artin identity fails, or a cabled P4 whose bundle strands are not conjugated by the conjugators evaluated on reverse-order bundle products.

A two-bridge knot b(4m^2+1, 2m) built from the formula with roots other than t0, 1/t0 or with a nonvanishing local form, or a (k,1)-cable of T(2,p) with roots off t^k = -1 or with a nonvanishing local form.
An algebra in the examples whose edge weight satisfies f(0, s*) = 0 or f(0, s*) = f(0) for every s* detecting its near triple.
foundation_claim_scope: p >= 5, r | p - 1, graded nilpotent Lie algebras of class at most 4 with a grading-preserving C_r action; manifolds S^3_(d/p)(K) (H1 = Z/d). Cited, not reproved: Bulatov-Grohe (via Cai-Chen-Lu Thm 2.1 and Cor 2.1); Schur-Zassenhaus; Lazard; Schubert's classification of two-bridge knots; the satellite formula for Alexander polynomials; universal coefficients over F_p[t, 1/t]; the anchor-isolation Lemma I of CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001C. Not covered: pair failures in classes 3 and 4 (the remaining case of the dichotomy), classes at least 5, non-graded algebras, p = 2, 3, knot exteriors. r counts the characters of the action, not Boolean variables. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: on seven pair quotients of free graded algebras every triple failure is near and every nonzero monomial of degree <= 4 in odd elements obeys parity; the Squier form J_t is Burau-invariant over Z[t, 1/t] for n <= 7 and mod p for n <= 12, with the bundle identity and J_t^T 1; the reversed Artin identity holds on 60 of 60 random braids and the forward one fails on 57; b(4m^2+1, 2m) has Alexander polynomial -m^2(t + 1/t) + 2m^2 + 1 (m <= 5) and the knots built from the formula at odd-order roots (p = 7, 13, 11, 19, 29) have cohomology exactly at t0^(+-1) and never obstruct (three algebras); (k,1)-cables of T(2,p) at seven (p, d, k) have cohomology exactly at t^k = -1 and never obstruct (four algebras, one pair-failing); cable_d(P4) acts by the conjugators on reverse-order bundle products for d = 2..6; exact edge-weight counts satisfy 0 < f(0, s*) < f(0) in six cases (4753 at p = 7 for the four-way algebra, matching the independent review); gadget forms match on four replications; experiment COPRIME-DICHOTOMY-20261027-001B-E002 supported; no human or external review
